newsitem.title: GERMANY: Support for Kohl falls further in June, poll finds.
newsitem.headline: Support for Kohl falls further in June, poll finds.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's popularity slipped further in the last month and he now trails a leading challenger from the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) by a two-to-one margin, a survey published on Friday said.

Gerhard Schroeder, premier of Lower Saxony state and the most popular of the SPD's possible candidates for chancellor, now has support from 60 percent of German voters, according to ZDF television's monthly Politbarometer survey of 1,332 people.
Only 30 percent of voters supported Kohl, the survey conducted by the Electoral Research Group found. That was down from 42 percent in May and 45 percent in April.
The survey said if an election were held on Sunday, 37 percent of voters would cast their ballots for Kohl's conservatives, down one point from May.
The telephone poll conducted between June 16 and June 19 found the SPD, Germany's leading opposition party, would receive 38 percent of the vote, unchanged from May.
The environmentalist Greens gained three points to 13 percent and the liberal Free Democrats, junior coalition partner to Kohl's conservatives, gained one point to six percent.
The reform communist Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS) was unchanged at four percent.
